name: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds

podcast.body: Featured on "The Transformed Man" album, Shatner performed this song out of its original context, which led to some confusion among listeners. He explained his interpretation of it as "LSD," a vision of tangerine trees and marmalade skies, performed as a "guy looped," contrasting with literary figures who achieve great heights without drugs. "People took things like Lucy and the Sky with Diamonds out of context. They were, what's he doing? Well, what I'm doing is performing LSD, a guy who thinks of tangering trees and marmalade skies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stop Me If You've Heard This One Before

podcast.body: Shatner performed this song on *The Transformed Man*, aiming to convey the vision of LSD by portraying "a guy looped," experiencing "change of injuries and marmalade skies." He intended this performance to contrast with the non-drug-influenced philosophical speech from Edmond Rostand's Cyrano. "Things like Lucy the Sky with Diamonds, out of context. Well, what's he doing? Well, what I'm doing is performing LSD, a guy who thinks of a change of, a change of injuries and marmalade skies. And that's LSD to me. That's a vision. And I try to perform it as a guy looped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
